claims.explanation: Levetiracetam's annotated targets are neuronal synaptic proteins (SV2A, CACNA1B, SCN1A), and its selective killing pattern tracks with neuroendocrine/neuronal-like lineage and NF2 loss rather than any canonical anticancer pathway. The most plausible mechanism is that levetiracetam engages SV2A/voltage-gated channel machinery that is aberrantly expressed or dependency-relevant in neuroendocrine, neural-crest, and NF2-mutant mesenchymal tumors, while lines with strong PI3K/MAPK/ARID1A-driven survival signaling are protected.

features.basis: NF2-mutant lines (NMCG1, YD8, SNU410, NCIH2052) are enriched among sensitive lines; NF2 loss is common in neural-crest/mesothelial tumors
SV2A is the validated levetiracetam binding target; expression in neuronal/neuroendocrine lines predicts engagement
Annotated levetiracetam target; N-type calcium channel expression may mediate sensitivity in neural lineages
Annotated levetiracetam target; voltage-gated sodium channel expression in excitable/neuronal-like tumors
BRAF-mutant lines (NMCG1, WM793, BCPAP, HEC265, CAL12T) appear among sensitive lines, suggesting MAPK-driven neural-crest dependency
PTEN loss is frequent in least-affected lines (ZR751, UACC62, H4, RL952, FTC238), suggesting PI3K survival signaling buffers drug effect
ARID1A-mutant lines (22RV1, OVTOKO, GP2D, RL952) are enriched among least-affected lines
KRAS-mutant lines (SW1573, NCIH1792, SNU81, GP2D) are overrepresented among resistant lines
TP53 mutation is near-universal in sensitive lines but also common in resistant lines, so weak alone; may cooperate with neural lineage
KMT2D mutations appear in several least-affected lines (RL952, 22RV1, GP2D, SNU81), suggesting chromatin-remodeling buffering
ATM mutations appear in resistant lines (ESS1, RL952) and sensitive lines (TE9, SNU685), so weak; listed for completeness
POLE mutation in NCIH2126 (most sensitive) and ESS1 (resistant) gives conflicting evidence; weak
